positioning: The forest cat of the far north.
story: The Norwegian Forest Cat looks built for winter, and it was. A waterproof top coat sheds the snow. A woolly undercoat holds the heat. A thick ruff and a long, bushy tail finish the job. In Norway it is the skogkatt, the forest cat.

Where it came from is still a good argument. Some say Viking ships carried its ancestors. Some say traders brought longhaired cats up from the south. Norse myth gave the goddess Freya a chariot pulled by two great cats, and fans of the breed have claimed them ever since.

What is certain is the farm. For centuries these cats worked barns and cottages, keeping mice out of the grain and themselves out of the cold. They climbed rock, trees, and rooftops. Few cats are better built for it.

A cat show in 1938 introduced the breed to the public, and a club formed in Oslo. Then the war nearly erased it. Breeders rebuilt the line with patience. King Olav V is said to have named it the official cat of Norway in the 1950s.
The breed took its time crossing the ocean. The Cat Fanciers' Association gave it full championship status in 1993.

Today the Norwegian Forest Cat is a big, gentle, unhurried companion. It takes up to five years to grow into itself. It will follow you to the window, watch the snow with you, and leave paw prints on every cold surface in the house.
fblocks: Skogkatt is Norwegian for forest cat. Fans call the breed Wegie for short.
King Olav V is said to have given the breed that title in the 1950s.
Slow to mature. Loves to climb, so give it height. Brush weekly, and daily in spring shedding. Ask the breeder about heart and genetic screening.
A long, water-resistant coat over a woolly undercoat, with a ruff, britches, and a bushy tail. Nearly every color and pattern, with or without white.
Up to 16 pounds. Up to 5 years to mature. CFA championship status in 1993. Ranked 13th by CFA registrations in 2023.
days: The Norwegian Forest Cat wears a waterproof coat over a wool undercoat.
Norse myth gave the goddess Freya a chariot pulled by two giant cats.
It takes up to five years to reach full size and full glory.
Nothing says winter like a Wegie asleep in the hay, tail over its nose.
The best seat in the barn is the doorway, with a view and no wind.
King Olav V is said to have made it Norway's official cat. Ask your friends.
After the snow and the chores, a Wegie tucks in one paw and sleeps.
last_walk:
The path is white and the cabin light is on.
A Norwegian Forest Cat has crossed this snow a thousand times. It walks without hurry, tail high, as if the forest were its own front yard. When it reaches the door, it does not ask to come in. It waits, because it knows the warm room is already waiting for it.
